title.zh: 卷七十一 志第二十二: 禮樂五
title.raw: 卷七十一 志第二十二: 禮樂五 Volume 71 Treatises 24: Rites and Music 5

sentences.zh: 禮樂五 ○樂服樂正副四人，舒腳襆頭，紫羅公服，烏角帶，木笏，皂靴。

translations.literal: Rites and Music 5 ○ Music Attire: Four chief and vice music directors, spread-foot turbans, purple gauze official robes, black horn belts, wooden court tablets, and black boots.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and Music 5 — Music Attire: The four chief and vice directors of music wore spread-foot turbans, purple gauze official robes, black horn belts, wooden court tablets, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 照燭二人，服同前，無笏。

translations.literal: Two lamp attendants, attire the same as before, without tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Two lamp attendants wore the same dress as above but carried no court tablets.

sentences.zh: 樂師二人，服緋，冠、笏同前。

translations.literal: Two music masters, scarlet attire, caps and tablets the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: Two music masters wore scarlet robes, with caps and tablets as described above.

sentences.zh: 運譜二人，服綠，冠、笏同前。

translations.literal: Two score carriers, green attire, caps and tablets the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: Two score carriers wore green robes, with caps and tablets as before.

sentences.zh: 舞師二人，舒腳襆頭，黃羅繡抹額，紫服，金銅荔枝帶，皂靴，各執仗。

translations.literal: Two dance masters, spread-foot turbans, yellow gauze embroidered forehead bands, purple robes, gold and bronze lychee-pattern belts, black boots, each holding a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Two dance masters wore spread-foot turbans, yellow gauze embroidered forehead bands, purple robes, gold-and-bronze lychee-pattern belts, and black boots, each bearing a ceremonial staff.

sentences.zh: （仗，牙仗也。）〉

translations.literal: (The staff is an ivory ceremonial staff.)
translations.idiomatic: (The staff is an ivory ceremonial staff.)

sentences.zh: 執旌二人，平冕，前後各九旒五就，青生色鸞袍，黃綾帶，黃絹袴，白絹襪，赤革履。

translations.literal: Two banner bearers, level caps, nine tassels and five clusters before and behind, blue unprocessed-color phoenix-pattern robes, yellow gauze belts, yellow silk trousers, white silk socks, and red leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Two banner bearers wore level caps with nine tassels and five clusters fore and aft, blue phoenix-pattern robes in the raw dye, yellow gauze belts, yellow silk trousers, white silk socks, and red leather shoes.

sentences.zh: （平冕鸞袍，皆仿金制，惟冕之旒數不同，詳見後至元二年博士議。）〉

translations.literal: (The level cap and phoenix-pattern robe both follow Jin regulations, but the number of cap tassels differs; see the deliberation of the Erudites in the second year of Zhiyuan, below.)
translations.idiomatic: (Both the level cap and the phoenix-pattern robe followed Jin practice, though the number of tassels on the cap differed; see the Erudites' ruling of the second year of Zhiyuan, below.)

sentences.zh: 執纛二人，青羅巾，余同執旌。

translations.literal: Two standard bearers, blue gauze caps; the rest the same as the banner bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Two standard bearers wore blue gauze caps; all else matched the banner bearers.

sentences.zh: 樂工，介幘冠，緋羅生色鸞袍，黃綾帶，皂靴。

translations.literal: Musicians: leveled caps, scarlet gauze unprocessed-color phoenix-pattern robes, yellow gauze belts, black boots.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians wore leveled caps, scarlet gauze phoenix-pattern robes in the raw dye, yellow gauze belts, and black boots.

sentences.zh: （冠以皮為之，黑油如熊耳，亦金制也。）〉

translations.literal: (The cap is made of leather, blackened like bear ears; this too follows Jin regulations.)
translations.idiomatic: (The cap was of leather, blackened like bear ears; this too followed Jin practice.)

sentences.zh: 歌工，服同樂工。

translations.literal: Singers: attire the same as musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Singers wore the same dress as the musicians.

sentences.zh: 執麾，服同上，惟加平巾幘。

translations.literal: Banner conductors: attire as above, only adding a flat-cloth cap.
translations.idiomatic: Banner conductors dressed as above but also wore a flat-cloth cap.

sentences.zh: （狀若籠金幘，以革為之。）〉

translations.literal: (Shaped like a gilded cage-cap, made of leather.)
translations.idiomatic: (Shaped like a gilded cage-cap and made of leather.)

sentences.zh: 舞人，青羅生色義花鸞袍，緣以皂綾，平冕冠。

translations.literal: Dancers: blue gauze unprocessed-color righteousness-flower phoenix-pattern robes, bordered with black gauze, level caps.
translations.idiomatic: Dancers wore blue gauze phoenix-pattern robes patterned with righteousness flowers in the raw dye, trimmed in black gauze, and level caps.

sentences.zh: （冠前後有旒，青白硝石珠相間。）〉

translations.literal: (The cap has tassels before and behind, blue and white saltpeter beads alternating.)
translations.idiomatic: (The cap bore tassels fore and aft, strung with alternating blue and white saltpeter beads.)

sentences.zh: 執器二十人，服同樂工，綠油母追冠，

translations.literal: Twenty instrument bearers, attire the same as musicians, green-oiled leather military caps,
translations.idiomatic: Twenty instrument bearers dressed like the musicians and wore green-oiled leather military caps,

sentences.zh: （革為之，一名武弁。）〉

translations.literal: (Made of leather; also called a martial cap.)
translations.idiomatic: (Made of leather and also known as a martial cap.)

sentences.zh: 加紅抹額。

translations.literal: With red forehead bands added.
translations.idiomatic: With red forehead bands added.

sentences.zh: 至元二年閏五月，大樂署言，堂上下樂舞官員及樂工，合用衣服冠冕靴履等物，乞行制造。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, the Office of Great Music reported that the music and dance officers above and below the hall and the musicians required robes, caps, crowns, boots, shoes, and the like, and requested that manufacture be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, the Office of Great Music reported that the music and dance officers in the upper and lower halls and all the musicians needed robes, caps, crowns, boots, and shoes, and asked that these be made.

sentences.zh: 太常寺下博士議定：樂正副四人、樂師二人、照燭二人、運譜二人，皆服紫羅公服，皂紗襆頭舒腳，紅鞓角帶，木笏，皂靴。

translations.literal: The Erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated and fixed: four chief and vice music directors, two music masters, two lamp attendants, and two score carriers all wore purple gauze official robes, black gauze spread-foot turbans, red-trim horn belts, wooden tablets, and black boots.
translations.idiomatic: The Erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ruled that the four chief and vice directors, two music masters, two lamp attendants, and two score carriers should all wear purple gauze official robes, black gauze spread-foot turbans, red-trim horn belts, wooden court tablets, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 引舞色長四人，紫羅公服，皂紗襆頭展腳，黃羅繡南花抹額，金銅帶，皂靴。

translations.literal: Four lead-dance section chiefs: purple gauze official robes, black gauze extended-foot turbans, yellow gauze embroidered southern-flower forehead bands, gold and bronze belts, black boots.
translations.idiomatic: Four lead-dance section chiefs wore purple gauze official robes, black gauze extended-foot turbans, yellow gauze forehead bands embroidered with southern flowers, gold-and-bronze belts, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 樂工二百四十有六人，緋繡義花鸞袍，縣黃插口，介幘冠，紫羅帶，全黃羅抹帶，黃絹夾褲，白綾襪，朱履。

translations.literal: Two hundred forty-six musicians: scarlet embroidered righteousness-flower phoenix-pattern robes, yellow insertion panels hanging down, leveled caps, purple gauze belts, full yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred forty-six musicians wore scarlet embroidered phoenix-pattern robes with righteousness flowers, yellow hanging insertion panels, leveled caps, purple gauze belts, full yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: （金太常寺掌故張珍所著《疊代世範》載金制：舞人服黑衫，皆四襖，有黃插口，左右垂之，黃綾抹帶，其衫以綢為之，胸背二答、兩肩二答，前後和一答，皆彩色，繡二鸞盤飛之狀，綴之於衫。

translations.literal: (Zhang Zhen, an archivist of the Jin Court of Imperial Sacrifices, records in his Successive Ages as Models the Jin regulations: dancers wore black jackets, all of four layers, with yellow insertion panels hanging down left and right, yellow gauze forehead bands; the jackets were of silk, with two panels on chest and back, two on each shoulder, and one joining front and back, all in colors, embroidered with two phoenixes coiling in flight, affixed to the jacket.)
translations.idiomatic: (In Zhang Zhen's Successive Ages as Models, an archivist of the Jin Court of Imperial Sacrifices records Jin practice: dancers wore black four-layer jackets with yellow insertion panels hanging at either side, yellow gauze forehead bands, and silk coats bearing colored panels on chest, back, and shoulders—seven panels in all—each embroidered with paired phoenixes in flight and sewn to the garment.)

sentences.zh: 冠以平冕，亦有天板、口圈，天門納言以紫絹標背，銅裹邊圈，前後各五旒，以青白硝石珠相間。

translations.literal: The cap was a level crown, also with a heaven board and mouth ring; the Gate of Heaven and Reception of Words were marked on purple silk backing, the rim wrapped in copper, five tassels before and behind, blue and white saltpeter beads alternating.
translations.idiomatic: They wore level crowns with heaven boards and mouth rings; the Gate of Heaven and Reception of Words were marked on purple silk backing, the rim copper-clad, with five tassels fore and aft strung with alternating blue and white saltpeter beads.

sentences.zh: 《大備集》所載，二舞人皂繡義花鸞衫，縣紫插口，黃綾抹帶，朱履，平冕。

translations.literal: As recorded in the Comprehensive Rites Collection, two dancers wore black embroidered righteousness-flower phoenix jackets, purple insertion panels hanging down, yellow gauze forehead bands, red shoes, level crowns.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Rites Collection records two dancers in black embroidered phoenix jackets with righteousness flowers, purple hanging insertion panels, yellow gauze forehead bands, red shoes, and level crowns.

sentences.zh: 其冠有口圈，亦有天門納言系帶，口圈高一尺許，天板長二尺，闊一尺，前微高後低，裏外紫絹糊，銅楞道妝釘，無旒。）〉

translations.literal: Their crowns had mouth rings and also Gate of Heaven and Reception of Words fastening straps; the mouth ring was about one foot high, the heaven board two feet long and one foot wide, slightly higher in front and lower behind, lined inside and out with purple silk, copper ribs and decorative nails, without tassels.)
translations.idiomatic: Their crowns had mouth rings and straps for the Gate of Heaven and Reception of Words; the mouth ring stood about a foot high, the heaven board two feet long and one foot wide, slightly higher in front, lined with purple silk inside and out, ribbed and studded with copper, and bore no tassels.)

sentences.zh: 執器二十人，緋繡義花鸞袍，縣黃插口，綠油革冠，黃羅抹帶，黃絹夾褲，白綾襪，朱履。

translations.literal: Twenty instrument bearers: scarlet embroidered righteousness-flower phoenix-pattern robes, yellow insertion panels hanging down, green-oiled leather caps, yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty instrument bearers wore scarlet embroidered phoenix-pattern robes with righteousness flowers, yellow hanging insertion panels, green-oiled leather caps, yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: 旌纛四人，青繡義花鸞袍，縣紫插口，平冕冠二，青包巾二，黃羅抹帶，黃絹夾褲，白綾襪，朱履。

translations.literal: Four banner and standard bearers: blue embroidered righteousness-flower phoenix-pattern robes, purple insertion panels hanging down, two level crowns, two blue wrapped caps, yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Four banner and standard bearers wore blue embroidered phoenix-pattern robes with righteousness flowers and purple hanging insertion panels; two wore level crowns and two blue wrapped caps, with yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: 七月，中書吏部再準太常博士議定，行下所司制造。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Secretariat and Ministry of Personnel again approved the deliberation of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudites and issued orders to the relevant offices to manufacture them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Secretariat and Ministry of Personnel again ratified the Erudites' ruling and directed the appropriate offices to manufacture the items.

sentences.zh: 三年九月服成，緋鸞袍二百六十有七，青鸞袍一百三十二，黃絹褲一百五十二，紫羅公服一十四，黃綾帶三百九十七，介幘冠二百四十有四，平冕冠百三十，簪全，木笏十有六，襆頭十有四，平巾幘二，綠油革冠二十，荔枝銅帶四，角帶十，皂靴二百六十對，朱履百五十對。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year the garments were completed: two hundred sixty-seven scarlet phoenix-pattern robes, one hundred thirty-two blue phoenix-pattern robes, one hundred fifty-two yellow silk trousers, fourteen purple gauze official robes, three hundred ninety-seven yellow gauze belts, two hundred forty-four leveled caps, one hundred thirty level crowns, hairpins complete, sixteen wooden tablets, fourteen turbans, two flat-cloth caps, twenty green-oiled leather caps, four lychee-pattern bronze belts, ten horn belts, two hundred sixty pairs of black boots, one hundred fifty pairs of red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month of the third year the garments were finished: 267 scarlet phoenix-pattern robes, 132 blue phoenix-pattern robes, 152 yellow silk trousers, 14 purple gauze official robes, 397 yellow gauze belts, 244 leveled caps, 130 level crowns with hairpins, 16 wooden court tablets, 14 turbans, 2 flat-cloth caps, 20 green-oiled leather caps, 4 lychee-pattern bronze belts, 10 horn belts, 260 pairs of black boots, and 150 pairs of red shoes.

sentences.zh: 宣聖廟樂工，黑漆冠三十五，綠羅生色胸背花袍三十五，皂靴三十五對，黃絹囊三十五，黃絹夾袱三十五。

translations.literal: Musicians at the Temple of the Exalted Sage: thirty-five black lacquered caps, thirty-five green gauze unprocessed-color chest-and-back floral robes, thirty-five pairs of black boots, thirty-five yellow silk pouches, thirty-five yellow silk lined wrappers.
translations.idiomatic: For musicians at the Temple of the Exalted Sage there were 35 black lacquered caps, 35 green gauze robes with floral chest-and-back panels in the raw dye, 35 pairs of black boots, 35 yellow silk pouches, and 35 yellow silk lined wrappers.

sentences.zh: 大樂職掌

translations.literal: Duties of Great Music
translations.idiomatic: Duties of Great Music

sentences.zh: 大樂署，令一人，丞一人，掌郊社、宗廟之樂。

translations.literal: The Office of Great Music had one director and one vice director, in charge of music for suburban altars and the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Great Music had one director and one deputy, charged with music for suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 凡樂，郊社、宗廟則用宮縣，工四百六十有一人；

translations.literal: For music generally, suburban altars and the ancestral temple used the palace suspended ensemble, four hundred sixty-one workers;
translations.idiomatic: For suburban altars and the ancestral temple the palace suspended ensemble was used, with 461 musicians;

sentences.zh: 社稷，則用登歌，工五十有一人；

translations.literal: For the altars of soil and grain, elevated singing was used, fifty-one workers;
translations.idiomatic: for the altars of soil and grain, elevated singing, with 51 musicians;

sentences.zh: 二樂用工三百一十有二人，代事故者五十人。

translations.literal: The two kinds of music together employed three hundred twelve workers, with fifty substitutes for vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: both forms together required 312 musicians, with 50 substitutes to cover vacancies.

sentences.zh: 前祭之月，召工習樂及舞。

translations.literal: In the month before the sacrifice, workers were summoned to practice music and dance.
translations.idiomatic: In the month before a sacrifice, musicians were summoned to rehearse the music and dances.

sentences.zh: 祀前一日，宿縣於庭中。

translations.literal: On the day before the sacrifice, the suspended ensemble lodged overnight in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the rite the suspended ensemble was set up and kept overnight in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 東方西方設十二镈鐘，各依辰位。

translations.literal: East and west were set with twelve bo bells, each according to its earthly-branch position.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve bo bells were placed east and west, each aligned to its earthly-branch station.

sentences.zh: 編鐘處其左，編磬處其右。

translations.literal: The serial bells were placed to their left, the serial chimes to their right.
translations.idiomatic: Serial bells stood to their left and serial chimes to their right.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之鐘起子位，在通街之西。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell bell began at the zi position, west of the main thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell bell began at the zi station, west of the main thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓之鐘居午位，在通街之東。

translations.literal: The Flourishing Guest bell occupied the wu position, east of the main thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: The Flourishing Guest bell stood at the wu station, east of the main thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 每辰三虡，謂之一肆，十有二辰，凡三十六虡。

translations.literal: Each earthly branch had three stands, called one array; twelve branches in all, thirty-six stands altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Each earthly-branch station had three stands, forming one array; across twelve stations there were thirty-six stands in all.

sentences.zh: 樹建鞞應於四隅，左右，設縣中之北。

translations.literal: Side drums and answering drums were erected at the four corners; left and right, set north of the center of the suspended ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: Side drums and answering drums were set at the four corners; to left and right they stood north of the center of the suspended ensemble.

sentences.zh: 歌工次之，

translations.literal: Singers came next,
translations.idiomatic: Next came the singers,

sentences.zh: （三十二人，重行相向而坐。）〉

translations.literal: (Thirty-two persons, seated in double rows facing one another.)
translations.idiomatic: (Thirty-two singers seated in double rows facing one another.)

sentences.zh: 巢笙次之，簫次之，竽次之，籥次之，篪次之，塤次之，長笛又次之。

translations.literal: Nest panpipes came next, then vertical flutes, then mouth organs, then transverse flutes, then bamboo flutes, then globular flutes, then long flutes again after.
translations.idiomatic: Then came nest panpipes, vertical flutes, mouth organs, transverse flutes, bamboo flutes, globular flutes, and finally long flutes.

sentences.zh: 夾街之左右，瑟翼敔之東西，在前行。

translations.literal: Flanking the thoroughfare left and right, zithers flanked the clappers east and west, in the front row.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking the thoroughfare, zithers stood east and west of the clappers in the front rank.

sentences.zh: 路鼓、路鼗次之。

translations.literal: Road drums and road hand-drums came next.
translations.idiomatic: Road drums and road tambourines came next.

sentences.zh: （郊祀則雷鼓、雷鼗。）〉

translations.literal: (For suburban sacrifices, thunder drums and thunder tambourines.)
translations.idiomatic: (At suburban sacrifices, thunder drums and thunder tambourines were used.)

sentences.zh: 閏余匏在簫之東，七星匏在西，九曜匏次之。

translations.literal: The Intercalary Remainder gourd was east of the vertical flute, the Seven Stars gourd to the west, the Nine Luminaries gourd next.
translations.idiomatic: The Intercalary Remainder gourd stood east of the vertical flute, the Seven Stars gourd to the west, then the Nine Luminaries gourd.

sentences.zh: 一弦琴列路鼓之東西，

translations.literal: One-string zithers were arrayed east and west of the road drums,
translations.idiomatic: One-string zithers were placed east and west of the road drums,

sentences.zh: （東一，西二。）〉

translations.literal: (One to the east, two to the west.)
translations.idiomatic: (one on the east, two on the west.)

sentences.zh: 三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦次之。

translations.literal: Three-string, five-string, seven-string, and nine-string came next.
translations.idiomatic: Followed by three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers.

sentences.zh: 晉鼓一，處縣中之東南，以節樂。

translations.literal: One Jin drum, placed southeast of the center of the suspended ensemble, to mark the beat of the music.
translations.idiomatic: A single Jin drum stood southeast of the center of the ensemble to mark the beat.

sentences.zh: （一弦琴三，五弦以下皆六。

translations.literal: (Three one-string zithers; from five-string down, six each.
translations.idiomatic: (Three one-string zithers; from the five-string type downward, six of each.

sentences.zh: 凡坐者，高以杌，地以氈。）〉

translations.literal: All who sat used stools for height and felt for the ground.)
translations.idiomatic: Those who sat used stools for elevation and felt mats on the ground.)

sentences.zh: 立四表於橫街之南，少東。

translations.literal: Four markers were erected south of the cross-street, slightly east.
translations.idiomatic: Four markers were set up south of the cross-street, slightly to the east.

sentences.zh: 設舞位於縣北。

translations.literal: Dance positions were set north of the suspended ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: Dance positions were laid out north of the suspended ensemble.

sentences.zh: 文郎左執籥，右秉翟；

translations.literal: Civil dancers held flutes in the left hand and grasped feathers in the right;
translations.idiomatic: Civil dancers held flutes in the left hand and pheasant feathers in the right;

sentences.zh: 武郎左執幹，右執戚；

translations.literal: Martial dancers held shields in the left hand and axes in the right;
translations.idiomatic: Martial dancers held shields in the left hand and battle-axes in the right;

sentences.zh: 皆六十有四人。

translations.literal: Sixty-four in all.
translations.idiomatic: sixty-four in all.

sentences.zh: 享日，與工人先入就位。

translations.literal: On the day of the offering, they entered with the workers first and took their positions.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the offering they entered ahead of the musicians and took their places.

sentences.zh: 舞師二人，執纛二人，引文舞分立於表南。

translations.literal: Two dance masters, two standard bearers, leading the civil dance to stand separately south of the markers.
translations.idiomatic: Two dance masters and two standard bearers led the civil dancers to stand in formation south of the markers.

sentences.zh: 武舞及執器者，俟立於宮縣之左右。

translations.literal: The martial dance and instrument bearers waited, standing to left and right of the palace suspended ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: The martial dancers and instrument bearers waited on either side of the palace suspended ensemble.

sentences.zh: 器鼗二，雙鐸二，單鐸二，鐃二，錞二，

translations.literal: Two instrument tambourines, two paired bells, two single bells, two cymbals, two gongs,
translations.idiomatic: Two instrument tambourines, two paired bells, two single bells, two cymbals, and two gongs,

sentences.zh: （二錞用六人。）〉

translations.literal: (Two gongs required six persons.)
translations.idiomatic: (The two gongs required six players.)

sentences.zh: 鉦二，相鼓二，雅鼓二，凡二十人。

translations.literal: Two chimes, two phase drums, two elegant drums, twenty persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: Two chimes, two phase drums, two elegant drums—twenty players in all.

sentences.zh: 文舞退，舞師二人、執旌二人，引武舞進，立其處，文舞還立於縣側。

translations.literal: When the civil dance withdrew, two dance masters and two banner bearers led the martial dance forward to stand in their place; the civil dance returned to stand beside the suspended ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil dance withdrew, two dance masters and two banner bearers led the martial dancers forward to take their place, while the civil dancers returned to stand beside the suspended ensemble.

sentences.zh: 又設登歌樂於殿之前楹，

translations.literal: Elevated singing music was also set before the front columns of the hall,
translations.idiomatic: Elevated singing was also arranged before the front columns of the hall,

sentences.zh: （殿陛之旁，設樂床二，樂工列於上。）〉

translations.literal: (Beside the hall steps, two music platforms were set, musicians arrayed upon them.)
translations.idiomatic: (beside the hall steps, with two music platforms and musicians arrayed upon them.)

sentences.zh: 搏拊二，歌工六，一，一，在門內，相向而坐。

translations.literal: Two clappers, six singers, one and one, inside the gate, seated facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: With two clappers and six singers—three on each side inside the gate, seated facing one another.

sentences.zh: 鐘一虡，在前楹之東。

translations.literal: One stand of bells, east of the front columns.
translations.idiomatic: One bell stand stood east of the front columns.

sentences.zh: 一弦、三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦琴五，次之。

translations.literal: Five one-string, three-string, five-string, seven-string, and nine-string zithers came next.
translations.idiomatic: Followed by one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, five in all.

sentences.zh: 瑟二，在其東，笛一、籥一、篪一在琴之南，巢笙、和笙各二次之。

translations.literal: Two zithers, east of them; one flute, one transverse flute, one bamboo flute south of the zithers; nest panpipes and harmony panpipes, two of each, came next.
translations.idiomatic: Two zithers stood to their east; a flute, transverse flute, and bamboo flute south of the zithers; then two nest panpipes and two harmony panpipes.

sentences.zh: 塤一，在笛之南。

translations.literal: One globular flute, south of the flute.
translations.idiomatic: A globular flute stood south of the flute.

sentences.zh: 閏余匏、排簫各一，次之，皆西上。

translations.literal: One Intercalary Remainder gourd and one panpipe organ, each next, all ascending to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Then came one Intercalary Remainder gourd and one panpipe organ, all ranked ascending toward the west.

sentences.zh: 磬一虡，在前楹之西。

translations.literal: One stand of chimes, west of the front columns.
translations.idiomatic: One chime stand stood west of the front columns.

sentences.zh: 一弦、三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦琴五，次之。

translations.literal: Five one-string, three-string, five-string, seven-string, and nine-string zithers came next.
translations.idiomatic: Followed by one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, five in all.

sentences.zh: 塤一，在笛之南。

translations.literal: One globular flute, south of the flute.
translations.idiomatic: A globular flute stood south of the flute.

sentences.zh: 七星匏、九曜匏、排簫各一，次之，皆東上。

translations.literal: One Seven Stars gourd, one Nine Luminaries gourd, one panpipe organ, each next, all ascending to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Then came one Seven Stars gourd, one Nine Luminaries gourd, and one panpipe organ, all ranked ascending toward the east.

sentences.zh: 凡宗廟之樂九成，舞九變。

translations.literal: For ancestral temple music in general, nine completions of music, nine transformations of dance.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple music comprised nine movements, with nine dance transformations.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之宮，三成，三變。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell mode: three completions, three transformations.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell mode: three movements and three dance transformations.

sentences.zh: 大呂之角，二成，二變。

translations.literal: Great Regulator angle: two completions, two transformations.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Regulator angle: two movements and two transformations.

sentences.zh: 太簇之徵，二成，二變。

translations.literal: Great Cluster mode: two completions, two transformations.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Cluster mode: two movements and two transformations.

sentences.zh: 應鐘之羽，二成，二變。

translations.literal: Responding Bell feather: two completions, two transformations.
translations.idiomatic: The Responding Bell feather: two movements and two transformations.

sentences.zh: 圜丘之樂六成，舞六變。

translations.literal: Music for the Round Mound had six completions, six dance transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Music at the Round Mound comprised six movements and six dance transformations.

sentences.zh: 夾鐘之宮，三成，三變。

translations.literal: Bell Attached mode: three completions, three transformations.
translations.idiomatic: The Bell Attached mode: three movements and three transformations.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之角，一成，一變。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell angle: one completion, one transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell angle: one movement and one transformation.

sentences.zh: 太簇之徵，一成，一變。

translations.literal: Great Cluster mode: one completion, one transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Cluster mode: one movement and one transformation.

sentences.zh: 姑洗之羽，一成，一變。

translations.literal: Maiden Wash feather: one completion, one transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Maiden Wash feather: one movement and one transformation.

sentences.zh: 社稷之樂八成：林鐘之宮二成，太簇之角二成，姑洗之征二成，南呂之羽二成。

translations.literal: Music for the altars of soil and grain had eight completions: Forest Bell mode two completions, Great Cluster angle two completions, Maiden Wash mode two completions, Southern Regulator feather two completions.
translations.idiomatic: Altars-of-soil-and-grain music had eight movements: two in Forest Bell mode, two in Great Cluster angle, two in Maiden Wash mode, and two in Southern Regulator feather.

sentences.zh: 凡有事於宗廟，大樂令位於殿楹之東，西向；

translations.literal: Whenever there was business at the ancestral temple, the Director of Great Music took his position east of the hall columns, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rites were performed at the ancestral temple, the Director of Great Music stood east of the hall columns, facing west;

sentences.zh: 丞位於縣北，通街之東，西向；

translations.literal: the Vice Director at the north of the suspended ensemble, east of the main thoroughfare, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: the deputy stood north of the suspended ensemble, east of the main thoroughfare, facing west;

sentences.zh: 以肅樂舞。

translations.literal: to oversee the music and dance.
translations.idiomatic: to keep order over the music and dance.

sentences.zh: 協律郎二人，掌和律呂，以合陰陽之聲。

translations.literal: Two Pitch-Regulation Masters supervised harmonizing the pitch pipes to combine yin and yang tones.
translations.idiomatic: Two Pitch-Regulation Masters harmonized the pitch pipes so yin and yang tones might combine.

sentences.zh: 陽律六：黃鐘子，太簇寅，姑洗辰，蕤賓午，夷則申，無射戌。

translations.literal: The six yang pipes: Yellow Bell at zi, Great Cluster at yin, Maiden Wash at chen, Flourishing Guest at wu, Leveling Rule at shen, Unending Shot at xu.
translations.idiomatic: The six yang pipes: Yellow Bell at zi, Great Cluster at yin, Maiden Wash at chen, Flourishing Guest at wu, Leveling Rule at shen, and Unending Shot at xu.

sentences.zh: 陰呂六：大呂醜，夾鐘卯，仲呂巳，林鐘未，南呂酉，應鐘亥。

translations.literal: The six yin tubes: Great Regulator at chou, Bell Attached at mao, Second Bell at si, Forest Bell at wei, Southern Regulator at you, Responding Bell at hai.
translations.idiomatic: The six yin tubes: Great Regulator at chou, Bell Attached at mao, Second Bell at si, Forest Bell at wei, Southern Regulator at you, and Responding Bell at hai.

sentences.zh: 文之以宮、商、角、徵、羽、變宮、變徵，播之以金、石、絲、竹、匏、土、革、木。

translations.literal: They were patterned with gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu, altered gong, and altered zhi, and disseminated through metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, earth, leather, and wood.
translations.idiomatic: They were patterned with gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu, altered gong, and altered zhi, and sounded through metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, earth, leather, and wood.

sentences.zh: 凡律管之數九，九九相乘，八十一以為宮；

translations.literal: For pitch-pipe numbers in general, nine; nine multiplied by nine, eighty-one taken as gong;
translations.idiomatic: Pitch-pipe numbers totaled nine; nine times nine yielded eighty-one for gong;

sentences.zh: 三分去一，五十四以為徵；

translations.literal: one-third removed, fifty-four taken as zhi;
translations.idiomatic: one-third removed left fifty-four for zhi;

sentences.zh: 三分益一，七十二以為商；

translations.literal: one-third added, seventy-two taken as shang;
translations.idiomatic: one-third added yielded seventy-two for shang;

sentences.zh: 三分去一，四十八以為羽；

translations.literal: one-third removed, forty-eight taken as yu;
translations.idiomatic: one-third removed left forty-eight for yu;

sentences.zh: 三分益一，六十四以為角。

translations.literal: one-third added, sixty-four taken as jue.
translations.idiomatic: one-third added yielded sixty-four for jue.

sentences.zh: 如黃鐘為宮，則林鐘為徵，太簇為商，南呂為羽，姑洗為角，應鐘為變宮，蕤賓為變征，是為七聲十二律，還相為宮，為八十四調。

translations.literal: If Yellow Bell served as gong, then Forest Bell was zhi, Great Cluster was shang, Southern Regulator was yu, Maiden Wash was jue, Responding Bell was altered gong, Flourishing Guest was altered zhi—thus seven tones and twelve pipes, each cycling as gong, forming eighty-four modes.
translations.idiomatic: With Yellow Bell as gong, Forest Bell was zhi, Great Cluster shang, Southern Regulator yu, Maiden Wash jue, Responding Bell altered gong, and Flourishing Guest altered zhi—seven tones across twelve pipes, each cycling as gong to form eighty-four modes.

sentences.zh: 凡大祭祀皆法服，一人立於殿楹之西，東向；

translations.literal: For great sacrifices all wore ritual dress; one person stood west of the hall columns, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: At great sacrifices all wore ritual dress; one man stood west of the hall columns, facing east;

sentences.zh: 一人立於縣北通街之西，東向；

translations.literal: one person stood west of the main thoroughfare north of the suspended ensemble, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: another stood west of the main thoroughfare north of the suspended ensemble, facing east;

sentences.zh: 以節樂。

translations.literal: to mark the beat of the music.
translations.idiomatic: to mark the beat.

sentences.zh: （堂上者主登歌，堂下者主宮縣。）〉

translations.literal: (Those above the hall directed elevated singing; those below directed the palace suspended ensemble.)
translations.idiomatic: (Those in the upper hall directed elevated singing; those below directed the palace suspended ensemble.)

sentences.zh: 凡樂作，則跪，俯伏，舉麾以興，工鼓以奏；

translations.literal: Whenever music was performed, they knelt, prostrated themselves, raised the banner to begin, and the workers drummed to play;
translations.idiomatic: When music began they knelt and prostrated themselves, raised the banner to start, and the musicians drummed to play;

sentences.zh: 樂止則偃麾，工戛而樂止。

translations.literal: when the music stopped they lowered the banner, and the workers struck to halt the music.
translations.idiomatic: when it stopped they lowered the banner and the musicians struck to halt the music.

sentences.zh: （今執麾者代執之，協律郎特拜而已。）〉

translations.literal: (Today the banner conductor substitutes in holding it; the Pitch-Regulation Master only performs the special bow.)
translations.idiomatic: (Today the banner conductor holds it in their stead; the Pitch-Regulation Master performs only the special bow.)

sentences.zh: 樂正二人，副二人，掌肄樂舞、展樂器、正樂位。

translations.literal: Two chief music directors and two vice directors supervised rehearsing music and dance, displaying instruments, and correcting musical positions.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief directors and two deputies rehearsed music and dance, set out instruments, and corrected positions.

sentences.zh: 凡祭，二人立於殿內，二人立於縣間，以節樂。

translations.literal: At every sacrifice, two stood inside the hall and two between the suspended sets to mark the music.
translations.idiomatic: At every sacrifice two stood inside the hall and two between the suspended sets to mark the music.

sentences.zh: 殿內者視獻者奠獻用樂作止之節，以笏示照燭，照燭舉偃以示堂下。

translations.literal: Those inside watched the offering officer's presentation to begin and end the music, showing the tablet to the lamp attendants, who raised or lowered it to signal those below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those inside watched the offering officer's presentation and used their tablets to signal the lamp attendants, who raised or lowered their lamps to show those below.

sentences.zh: 若作登歌，則以笏示敔而已。

translations.literal: If elevated singing was performed, they showed the tablet only to the clapper player.
translations.idiomatic: For elevated singing they signaled only the clapper player.

sentences.zh: 縣間者視堂上照燭。

translations.literal: Those between the suspended sets watched the lamp attendants above the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those between the sets watched the hall lamp attendants.

sentences.zh: 及引初獻，照燭動，亦以笏示敔。

translations.literal: When leading the first offering, as the lamp attendants moved, they also showed the tablet to the clapper player.
translations.idiomatic: When leading the first offering, as the lamps moved they also signaled the clapper player.

sentences.zh: 樂師一人，運譜一人，掌以樂教工人。

translations.literal: One music master and one score carrier taught the workers through music.
translations.idiomatic: One music master and one score carrier taught the musicians.

sentences.zh: 凡祭，立於縣間，皆北上，相向而立。

translations.literal: At every sacrifice they stood between the suspended sets, all facing north above, standing opposite one another.
translations.idiomatic: At every sacrifice they stood between the sets, all facing north, opposite one another.

sentences.zh: 舞師四人，皆執梃，

translations.literal: Four dance masters, all holding staffs,
translations.idiomatic: Four dance masters, each holding a staff,

sentences.zh: （梃，牙仗也。）〉

translations.literal: (The staff is an ivory ceremonial staff.)
translations.idiomatic: (The staff is an ivory ceremonial staff.)

sentences.zh: 執纛二人，執旌二人，祭則前舉以為舞容。

translations.literal: two standard bearers, two banner bearers; at the sacrifice they advanced in front to set the dance formation.
translations.idiomatic: Two standard bearers and two banner bearers; at the sacrifice they advanced ahead to set the dance formation.

sentences.zh: 舞人從南表向第一表，為一成，則一變；

translations.literal: Dancers from the southern marker toward the first marker formed one completion, then one transformation;
translations.idiomatic: From the southern marker to the first marker counted as one movement and one transformation;

sentences.zh: 從第二至第三，為二成；

translations.literal: from the second to the third, two completions;
translations.idiomatic: from the second to the third, two movements;

sentences.zh: 從第三至北第四表，為三成；

translations.literal: from the third to the northern fourth marker, three completions;
translations.idiomatic: from the third to the northern fourth marker, three movements;

sentences.zh: 舞人各轉身南向於北表之北，還從第一至第二，為四成；

translations.literal: each dancer turned southward north of the northern marker, then returned from the first to the second, four completions;
translations.idiomatic: each dancer turned south beyond the northern marker, then returned from the first to the second for four movements;

sentences.zh: 從第二至第三，為五成；

translations.literal: from the second to the third, five completions;
translations.idiomatic: from the second to the third, five movements;

sentences.zh: 從第三至南第一表，為六成；

translations.literal: from the third to the southern first marker, six completions;
translations.idiomatic: from the third to the southern first marker, six movements;

sentences.zh: 若八變者，更從南北向第二，為七成；

translations.literal: for eight transformations, they again went from south to north to the second marker, seven completions;
translations.idiomatic: for eight transformations they went again from south to north to the second marker, seven movements;

sentences.zh: 又從第二至第三，為八成；

translations.literal: again from the second to the third, eight completions;
translations.idiomatic: again from the second to the third, eight movements;

sentences.zh: 若九變者，又從第三至北第一，為九變。

translations.literal: for nine transformations, again from the third to the northern first marker, nine transformations.
translations.idiomatic: for nine transformations, again from the third to the northern first marker, nine transformations.

sentences.zh: 執麾一人，從協律郎以麾舉偃而節樂。

translations.literal: One banner conductor followed the Pitch-Regulation Master, raising and lowering the banner to mark the music.
translations.idiomatic: One banner conductor followed the Pitch-Regulation Master, raising and lowering the banner to mark the music.

sentences.zh: 照燭二人，掌執籠燭而節樂。

translations.literal: Two lamp attendants supervised holding caged lamps to mark the music.
translations.idiomatic: Two lamp attendants held caged lamps to mark the music.

sentences.zh: 凡樂作止，皆舉偃其籠燭。

translations.literal: Whenever music began or stopped, they raised or lowered their caged lamps.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever music began or stopped, they raised or lowered their caged lamps.

sentences.zh: 一人立於堂上門東，視殿內獻官禮節，麾燭以示縣間。

translations.literal: One stood east of the upper hall gate, watching the offering officer's rites inside the hall, waving the lamp to signal those between the suspended sets.
translations.idiomatic: One stood east of the upper hall gate, watching the offering officer's rites and waving the lamp to signal those between the sets.

sentences.zh: 一人立於堂下縣間，俟三獻入導初獻至位，立於其左。

translations.literal: One stood between the suspended sets below the hall, waiting until the three offerings entered to guide the first offering to position, standing to his left.
translations.idiomatic: One stood between the sets below the hall and, when the three offerings entered, guided the first offering to position and stood at his left.

sentences.zh: （初獻行，皆前導，亞、終則否。）〉

translations.literal: (The first offering always had a forward guide; the second and final offerings did not.)
translations.idiomatic: (The first offering always had a forward guide; the second and final offerings did not.)

sentences.zh: 凡殿下禮節，則麾其燭以示上下。

translations.literal: For rites below the hall platform, they waved the lamp to signal above and below.
translations.idiomatic: For rites below the hall platform they waved the lamp to signal above and below.

sentences.zh: 初獻詣盥洗位，乃偃其燭，止亦如之。

translations.literal: When the first offering went to the washing stand, they lowered the lamp; stopping was the same.
translations.idiomatic: When the first offering went to the washing stand they lowered the lamp; halting was the same.

sentences.zh: 俟初獻動為節，宮縣樂作，詣盥洗位，洗拭瓚訖，樂止。

translations.literal: Waiting until the first offering moved as the signal, the palace suspended music played; he went to the washing stand, washed and wiped the libation vessel clean, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the first offering moved, the palace suspended music played; he went to the washing stand, washed and wiped the libation vessel, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 詣階，登歌樂作，升自東階，至殿門，樂止，乃立於陛側以俟。

translations.literal: He went to the steps; elevated singing played; he ascended the eastern steps to the hall gate, the music stopped, and he stood beside the steps to wait.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the steps; elevated singing played; he ascended the eastern steps to the hall gate; the music stopped and he stood beside the steps to wait.

sentences.zh: 晨稞訖，初獻出殿，登歌樂作，至版位，樂止。

translations.literal: When the morning offering was finished, the first offering left the hall; elevated singing played until he reached the position marker, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the morning offering was finished the first offering left the hall; elevated singing played until he reached the position marker, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 司徒迎饌至橫街，轉身北向，宮縣樂作，司徒奉俎至各室遍奠訖，樂止。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works met the offerings at the cross-street, turned northward, the palace suspended music played; the Minister bore the trays to each chamber and presented them throughout, then the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works met the offerings at the cross-street and turned north; palace suspended music played as he bore the trays to each chamber; when presentations were complete the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 酌獻，初獻詣盥洗位，宮縣樂作，詣爵洗位，洗拭爵訖，樂止。

translations.literal: For libation, the first offering went to the washing stand; palace suspended music played; he went to the wine-vessel washing stand, washed and wiped the cup clean, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: For libation the first offering went to the washing stand; palace suspended music played; he washed the cup at the wine-vessel stand and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 出笏，登歌樂作，升自東階，至殿門，樂止。

translations.literal: He produced his tablet; elevated singing played; he ascended the eastern steps to the hall gate, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He produced his tablet; elevated singing played; he ascended the eastern steps to the hall gate and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 初獻至酒尊所，酌訖，宮縣樂作，詣神位前，祭酒訖，拜、興、讀祝，樂止。

translations.literal: The first offering reached the wine vessels, poured, palace suspended music played; he went before the spirit seat, offered wine, bowed, rose, and read the prayer; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the wine vessels he poured; palace suspended music played; he went before the spirit seat, offered wine, bowed, rose, and read the prayer; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 讀訖，樂作，再拜訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, music played; when the second bow was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading ended music played; when the second bow ended the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次詣每室，作止如初。

translations.literal: Next he went to each chamber; beginning and stopping were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Next he went to each chamber with the same starts and stops.

sentences.zh: 每室各奏本室樂曲，俱獻畢，還至殿門，登歌樂作，降自東階，至版位，樂止。

translations.literal: Each chamber played that chamber's own tune; when all offerings were complete he returned to the hall gate; elevated singing played; he descended the eastern steps to the position marker, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Each chamber played its own tune; when all offerings were done he returned to the hall gate; elevated singing played as he descended the eastern steps to the position marker, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 文舞退，武舞進，宮縣樂作，舞者立定，樂止。

translations.literal: The civil dance withdrew, the martial dance advanced; palace suspended music played; the dancers stood fixed, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance withdrew and the martial dance advanced; palace suspended music played until the dancers stood fixed, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 亞獻行禮，無節步之樂，至酒尊所，酌酒訖，出笏，宮縣樂作，詣神位前，奠獻畢，樂止。

translations.literal: The second offering performed the rites without processional music; at the wine vessels, after pouring, he produced his tablet; palace suspended music played; he went before the spirit seat and completed the offering; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The second offering performed the rites without processional music; after pouring at the wine vessels he produced his tablet; palace suspended music played for the offering before the spirit seat, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 次詣每室，作止如初。

translations.literal: Next he went to each chamber; beginning and stopping were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Next he went to each chamber with the same starts and stops.

sentences.zh: 俱畢，還至版位，皆無樂。

translations.literal: When all were finished he returned to the position marker; there was no music.
translations.idiomatic: When all were finished he returned to the position marker without music.

sentences.zh: 終獻樂作，同亞獻，助奠以下升殿，奠馬湩，至神位，蒙古巫祝致詞訖，宮縣樂作，同司徒進饌之曲，禮畢，樂止。

translations.literal: The final offering's music played as for the second offering; assistants and below ascended the hall, presented mare's milk; at the spirit seat, after the Mongol shaman finished the invocation, palace suspended music played as for the Minister of Works bringing offerings; when the rite was complete the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The final offering's music matched the second; assistants ascended, presented mare's milk; at the spirit seat, after the Mongol shaman's invocation, palace suspended music played as when the Minister brought offerings; when the rite ended the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 出殿，登歌樂作，各復位，樂止。

translations.literal: Leaving the hall, elevated singing played; each returned to position, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the hall, elevated singing played until each returned to position, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 太祝徹籩豆，登歌樂作，卒徹，樂止。

translations.literal: The Grand Invoker removed the baskets and vessels; elevated singing played through the final clearing, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Invoker removed baskets and vessels; elevated singing played through the final clearing, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 奉禮贊拜，眾官皆再拜訖，送神，宮縣樂作，一成而止。

translations.literal: The Ceremonial Officer praised the bow; all officials bowed twice; seeing off the spirits, palace suspended music played one completion and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Officer led the bow; all officials bowed twice; for seeing off the spirits palace suspended music played one movement and stopped.

sentences.zh: 宴樂之器

translations.literal: Banquet Music Instruments
translations.idiomatic: Banquet Music Instruments

sentences.zh: 興隆笙，制以楠木，形如夾屏，上銳而面平，縷金雕鏤枇杷、寶相、孔雀、竹木、雲氣，兩旁側立花板，居背三之一，中為虛櫃，如笙之匏。

translations.literal: Prosperity-Flourishing panpipes, made of nanmu wood, shaped like a folding screen, sharp above and flat on the face, traced in gold with loquat, treasure-flower, peacock, bamboo, and cloud motifs; standing side panels on either flank, occupying one-third of the back, with a hollow cabinet in the center like a panpipe's gourd.
translations.idiomatic: The Prosperity-Flourishing panpipes were of nanmu, shaped like a folding screen, sharp above and flat-faced, gilded with loquat, treasure-flower, peacock, bamboo, and cloud motifs; side panels stood on either flank, one-third of the back, with a hollow cabinet at center like a panpipe gourd.

sentences.zh: 上豎紫竹管九十，管端實以木蓮苞。

translations.literal: Ninety purple bamboo pipes stood upright on it, their ends fitted with lotus-bud wood caps.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety purple bamboo pipes stood on it, capped with lotus-bud wood.

sentences.zh: 櫃外出小橛十五，上豎小管，管端實以銅杏葉。

translations.literal: Outside the cabinet fifteen small pegs projected, each bearing a small pipe capped with a bronze apricot leaf.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the cabinet fifteen small pegs bore small pipes capped with bronze apricot leaves.

sentences.zh: 下有座，獅象繞之，座上櫃前立花板一，雕鏤如背，板間出二皮風口，用則設朱漆小架於座前，系風囊於風口，囊面如琵琶，朱漆雜花，有柄，一人挼小管，一人鼓風囊，則簧自隨調而鳴。

translations.literal: Below was a stand encircled by lions and elephants; before the stand on the cabinet a panel was carved like the back; between the panels two leather wind mouths opened; when used, a vermilion lacquer small frame was set before the stand, wind bags tied to the mouths, their faces like pipa, vermilion lacquer with mixed flowers, with handles—one person plucked the small pipes, one person pumped the wind bag, and the reeds sounded according to the tuning.
translations.idiomatic: Below, a stand ringed with lions and elephants; before it a carved panel; between panels two leather wind mouths; in use a vermilion frame stood before the stand with wind bags at the mouths, faces like pipa in vermilion floral lacquer with handles—one plucked small pipes, one pumped the bag, and reeds sounded to the tuning.

sentences.zh: 中統間，回回國所進。

translations.literal: During the Zhongtong period it was presented by the Muslim lands.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhongtong period it was presented from the Muslim lands.

sentences.zh: 以竹為簧，有聲而無律。

translations.literal: Bamboo served as reeds; it had sound but no pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: Its reeds were bamboo; it sounded but had no standard pitch.

sentences.zh: 玉宸樂院判官鄭秀乃考音律，分定清濁，增改如今制。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiu, music officer of the Jade Hall Music Academy, examined pitch principles, distinguished clear and muddy tones, and revised it to the present form.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiu of the Jade Hall Music Academy examined pitch, sorted clear and muddy tones, and revised it to the present form.

sentences.zh: 其在殿上者，盾頭兩旁立刻木孔雀二，飾以真孔雀羽，中設機。

translations.literal: For those in the hall, on either side of the shield-heads two wooden peacocks were carved, adorned with real peacock feathers, with a mechanism set within.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall, flanking the shield-heads, two carved wooden peacocks adorned with real feathers held a mechanism within.

sentences.zh: 每奏，工三人，一人鼓風囊，一人按律，一人運動其機，則孔雀飛舞應節。

translations.literal: At each performance three workers: one pumped the wind bag, one held the pitch, one worked the mechanism, and the peacocks danced in time.
translations.idiomatic: At each performance three workers—one pumped the wind bag, one held pitch, one worked the mechanism—and the peacocks danced in time.

sentences.zh: 殿庭笙十，延祐間增制，不用孔雀。

translations.literal: Ten courtyard panpipes, added in the Yanyou period, without peacocks.
translations.idiomatic: Ten courtyard panpipes were added in the Yanyou period, without peacocks.

sentences.zh: 琵琶，制以木，曲首，長頸，四軫，頸有品，闊面，四弦，面飾雜花。

translations.literal: Pipa, made of wood, with curved head and long neck, four pegs, frets on the neck, broad face, four strings, the face decorated with mixed flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The pipa was wooden, with curved head, long neck, four pegs and frets, broad face, four strings, and a face decorated with mixed flowers.

sentences.zh: 箏，如瑟，兩頭微垂，有柱，十三弦。

translations.literal: Zheng, like the se zither, both ends slightly drooping, with bridges, thirteen strings.
translations.idiomatic: The zheng resembled the se, both ends slightly drooping, with bridges and thirteen strings.

sentences.zh: 火不思，制如琵琶，直頸，無品，有小槽，圓腹如半瓶榼，以皮為面，四弦，皮絣同一孤柱。

translations.literal: Huobusi, made like the pipa, straight neck, no frets, a small groove, round belly like half a bottle-gourd, leather face, four strings, the leather braced on a single arched bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The huobusi resembled the pipa but with straight neck and no frets, a small groove, round belly like half a bottle-gourd, leather face, four strings braced on one arched bridge.

sentences.zh: 胡琴，制如火不思，卷頸，龍首，二弦，用弓捩之，弓之弦以馬尾。

translations.literal: Huqin, made like the huobusi, curled neck, dragon head, two strings, played with a bow; the bow's string was of horsehair.
translations.idiomatic: The huqin resembled the huobusi with curled neck and dragon head, two strings bowed with a horsehair bowstring.

sentences.zh: 方響，制以鐵，十六枚，懸於磬虡，小角槌二。

translations.literal: Fangxiang, made of iron, sixteen pieces, suspended on a chime frame, two small-corner mallets.
translations.idiomatic: The fangxiang was iron, sixteen pieces on a chime frame, with two small-corner mallets.

sentences.zh: 廷中設，下施小交足幾，黃羅銷金衣。

translations.literal: Set in the courtyard on small crossed-leg tables, with yellow gauze gold-brocade covers.
translations.idiomatic: It was set in the courtyard on small crossed-leg tables under yellow gauze gold-brocade covers.

sentences.zh: 龍笛，制如笛，七孔，橫吹之，管首制龍頭，銜同心結帶。

translations.literal: Dragon flute, made like the transverse flute, seven holes, blown horizontally; the pipe head was carved as a dragon head holding a concentric knot band.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon flute resembled the transverse flute with seven holes, blown horizontally; the head was carved as a dragon holding a concentric knot band.

sentences.zh: 頭管，制以竹為管，卷蘆葉為首，竅七。

translations.literal: Touguan, made with bamboo pipe, reed-wrapped bulrush leaves for the head, seven holes.
translations.idiomatic: The touguan used a bamboo pipe with bulrush-wrapped head and seven holes.

sentences.zh: 笙，制以匏為底，列管於上，管十三，簧如之。

translations.literal: Sheng, made with gourd base, pipes arrayed above, thirteen pipes, reeds matching them.
translations.idiomatic: The sheng had a gourd base with thirteen pipes above and matching reeds.

sentences.zh: 箜篌，制以木，闊腹，腹下施橫木，而加軫二十四，柱頭及首並加鳳喙。

translations.literal: Konghou, made of wood, broad belly, a crossbar below the belly with twenty-four pegs, phoenix beaks on pillars and head.
translations.idiomatic: The konghou was wooden with broad belly, crossbar below bearing twenty-four pegs, phoenix beaks on pillars and head.

sentences.zh: 雲敖，制以銅，為小鑼十三，同一木架，下有長柄，左手持，而右手以小槌擊之。

translations.literal: Yun'ao, made of bronze as thirteen small gongs on one wooden frame, long handle below, held in the left hand and struck with a small mallet in the right.
translations.idiomatic: The yun'ao was bronze: thirteen small gongs on one frame with a long handle, held left-handed and struck right-handed with a small mallet.

sentences.zh: 簫，制如笛，五孔。

translations.literal: Xiao, made like the flute, five holes.
translations.idiomatic: The xiao resembled the flute with five holes.

sentences.zh: 戲竹，制如籈，長二尺餘，上系流蘇香囊，執而偃之，以止樂。

translations.literal: Xizhu, made like the chime-frame striker, more than two feet long, with tassel and incense pouch tied above, held and lowered to stop the music.
translations.idiomatic: The xizhu resembled a chime striker, over two feet long, with tassel and incense pouch tied above; held up and lowered to stop the music.

sentences.zh: 鼓，制以木為匡，冒以革，朱漆雜花，面繪復身龍，長竿二。

translations.literal: Drum, made with wooden frame, covered with leather, vermilion lacquer with mixed flowers, the face painted with coiled dragon, two long poles.
translations.idiomatic: The drum had a wooden frame covered with leather, vermilion lacquer with mixed flowers, a coiled dragon painted on the face, and two long poles.

sentences.zh: 廷中設，則有大木架，又有擊撾高座。

translations.literal: Set in the courtyard, there was a large wooden frame, and also a high seat for striking and beating.
translations.idiomatic: In the courtyard it stood on a large wooden frame with a high beating seat.

sentences.zh: 杖鼓，制以木為匡，細腰，以皮冒之，上施五彩繡帶，右擊以杖，左拍以手。

translations.literal: Zhang drum, made with wooden frame, narrow waist, covered with skin, with five-colored embroidered bands above; struck with a stick in the right hand, clapped with the left.
translations.idiomatic: The zhang drum had a wooden frame and narrow waist, skin-covered, with five-colored embroidered bands; struck right-handed with a stick, clapped left-handed.

sentences.zh: 劄鼓，制如杖鼓而小，左持而右擊之。

translations.literal: Zha drum, made like the zhang drum but smaller, held in the left hand and struck with the right.
translations.idiomatic: The zha drum resembled the zhang drum but smaller, held left-handed and struck right-handed.

sentences.zh: 和鼓，制如大鼓而小，左持而右擊之。

translations.literal: He drum, made like the large drum but smaller, held in the left hand and struck with the right.
translations.idiomatic: The he drum resembled the large drum but smaller, held left-handed and struck right-handed.

sentences.zh: 闉，制如箏而七弦，有柱，用竹軋之。

translations.literal: Yin, made like the zheng but with seven strings and bridges, played by rolling with bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: The yin resembled the zheng with seven strings and bridges, played by rolling with bamboo.

sentences.zh: 羌笛，制如笛而長，三孔。

translations.literal: Qiang flute, made like the flute but longer, three holes.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang flute resembled the flute but was longer, with three holes.

sentences.zh: 拍板，制以木為板，以繩聯之。

translations.literal: Clappers, made of wooden boards linked with cord.
translations.idiomatic: Clappers were wooden boards linked with cord.

sentences.zh: 水盞，制以銅，凡十有二，擊以鐵箸。

translations.literal: Water cups, made of bronze, twelve in all, struck with iron chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Water cups were bronze, twelve in all, struck with iron chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 樂音王隊：

translations.literal: Music-King Troupe:
translations.idiomatic: Music-King Troupe:

sentences.zh: （元旦用之。）〉

translations.literal: (Used at New Year's Day.)
translations.idiomatic: (Used on New Year's Day.)

sentences.zh: 引隊大樂禮官二員，冠展角襆頭，紫袍，塗金帶，執笏。

translations.literal: Leading the troupe, two Great Music ceremonial officers, wearing extended-foot turbans, purple robes, gilded belts, holding tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the troupe came two Great Music ceremonial officers in extended-foot turbans, purple robes, gilded belts, and tablets.

sentences.zh: 次執戲竹二人，同前服。

translations.literal: Next, two xizhu bearers, same dress as before.
translations.idiomatic: Next, two xizhu bearers in the same dress.

sentences.zh: 次樂工八人，冠花襆頭。

translations.literal: Next, eight musicians, wearing floral turbans.
translations.idiomatic: Next came eight musicians in floral turbans.

sentences.zh: 紫窄衫，銅束帶。

translations.literal: purple narrow-sleeved shirts, bronze belts.
translations.idiomatic: They wore purple narrow-sleeved shirts and bronze belts.

sentences.zh: 龍笛三，杖鼓三，金鞚小鼓一，板一，奏《萬年歡》之曲。

translations.literal: three dragon flutes, three zhang drums, one small golden bridle drum, one clapper board, performing the tune "Ten Thousand Years of Joy."
translations.idiomatic: They played three dragon flutes, three zhang drums, one small golden bridle drum, and one clapper, performing "Ten Thousand Years of Joy."

sentences.zh: 從東階升，至御前，以次而西，折繞而南，北向立。

translations.literal: They ascended from the eastern steps to before the emperor, in order westward, turned winding southward, and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: They ascended the eastern steps to the imperial presence, filed west in order, curved south, and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: （後隊進，皆仿此。）〉

translations.literal: (Later troupes entering all followed this pattern.)
translations.idiomatic: (Later troupes all followed this pattern.)

sentences.zh: 次二隊，婦女十人，冠展角襆頭，紫袍，隨樂聲進至御前，分左右相向立。

translations.literal: Next, the second troupe: ten women, wearing extended-foot turbans and purple robes, advanced with the music to before the emperor and stood facing one another left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The second troupe: ten women in extended-foot turbans and purple robes advanced with the music to the imperial presence and stood left and right facing one another.

sentences.zh: 次婦女一人，冠唐帽，黃袍，進北向立定，樂止，念致語畢，樂作，奏《長春柳》之曲。

translations.literal: Next one woman, wearing a Tang cap and yellow robe, advanced and stood facing north; the music stopped; when the congratulatory address was finished, music played, performing the tune "Long Spring Willow."
translations.idiomatic: Next one woman in a Tang cap and yellow robe advanced, stood facing north; music stopped; after the congratulatory address music played "Long Spring Willow."

sentences.zh: 次三隊，男子三人，戴紅發青面具，雜彩衣，次一人，冠唐帽，綠襕袍，角帶，舞蹈而進，立於前隊之右。

translations.literal: Next the third troupe: three men wearing red-haired green masks and mixed-color clothes; next one man wearing a Tang cap, green lined robe, and horn belt, dancing forward to stand to the right of the preceding troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The third troupe: three men in red-haired green masks and mixed-color clothes; then one man in a Tang cap, green lined robe, and horn belt danced forward to stand right of the preceding troupe.

sentences.zh: 次四隊，男子一人，戴孔雀明王像面具，披金甲，執叉，從者二人，戴毗沙神像面具，紅袍，執斧。

translations.literal: Next the fourth troupe: one man wearing a Peacock Bright King mask, clad in golden armor, holding a fork; two followers wearing Vaisravana masks, red robes, holding axes.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth troupe: one man in a Peacock Bright King mask, golden armor, holding a fork; two followers in Vaisravana masks, red robes, axes in hand.

sentences.zh: 次五隊，男子五人，冠五梁冠，戴龍王面具，繡氅，執圭，與前隊同進，北向立。

translations.literal: Next the fifth troupe: five men wearing five-ridged caps and Dragon King masks, embroidered mantles, holding scepters; they advanced like the preceding troupe and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth troupe: five men in five-ridged caps and Dragon King masks, embroidered mantles, scepters in hand, advanced like the preceding troupe and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 次六隊，男子五人，為飛天夜叉之像，舞蹈以進。

translations.literal: Next the sixth troupe: five men as flying yaksha images, dancing forward.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth troupe: five men as flying yaksha images danced forward.

sentences.zh: 次七隊，樂工八人，冠霸王冠，青面具，錦繡衣，龍笛三，觱栗三，杖鼓二，與前大樂合奏《吉利牙》之曲。

translations.literal: Next the seventh troupe: eight musicians wearing Conqueror caps and green masks, brocade embroidered clothes; three dragon flutes, three suona, two zhang drums, joining the preceding Great Music in performing the tune "Jiliya."
translations.idiomatic: The seventh troupe: eight musicians in Conqueror caps and green masks, brocade dress; three dragon flutes, three suona, two zhang drums, joining the Great Music in "Jiliya."

sentences.zh: 次八隊，婦女二十人，冠廣翠冠，銷金綠衣，執牡丹花，舞唱前曲，與樂聲相和，進至御前，北向，列為九重，重四人，曲終，再起，與後隊相和。

translations.literal: Next the eighth troupe: twenty women wearing broad kingfisher caps, gold-brocade green clothes, holding peony flowers, dancing and singing the preceding tune in harmony with the music, advancing to before the emperor facing north, arrayed in nine ranks of four each; when the tune ended they rose again to harmonize with the following troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth troupe: twenty women in broad kingfisher caps and gold-brocade green robes, peonies in hand, danced and sang the preceding tune, advanced to the imperial presence facing north in nine ranks of four; at the tune's end they rose again to meet the following troupe.

sentences.zh: 次九隊，婦女二十人，冠金梳翠花鈿，繡衣，執花鞚稍子鼓，舞唱前曲，與前隊相和。

translations.literal: Next the ninth troupe: twenty women wearing gold comb and kingfisher hairpins, embroidered clothes, holding flower-bridle slight drums, dancing and singing the preceding tune in harmony with the preceding troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth troupe: twenty women with gold comb and kingfisher hairpins, embroidered dress, flower-bridle slight drums, dancing and singing with the preceding troupe.

sentences.zh: 次十隊，婦女八人，花髻，服銷金桃紅衣，搖日月金鞚稍子鼓，舞唱同前。

translations.literal: Next the tenth troupe: eight women with floral topknots, wearing gold-brocade peach-pink clothes, shaking sun-and-moon golden bridle slight drums, dancing and singing as before.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth troupe: eight women with floral topknots in gold-brocade peach-pink robes, shaking sun-and-moon golden bridle slight drums, dancing and singing as before.

sentences.zh: 次男子五人，作五方菩薩梵像，搖日月鼓。

translations.literal: Next five men as Five-Direction Bodhisattva Sanskrit images, shaking sun-and-moon drums.
translations.idiomatic: Next five men as Five-Direction Bodhisattva Sanskrit images shook sun-and-moon drums.

sentences.zh: 次一人，作樂音王菩薩梵像，執花鞚稍子鼓，齊聲舞前曲一闋，樂止。

translations.literal: Next one man as the Music-King Bodhisattva Sanskrit image, holding a flower-bridle slight drum; all danced the preceding tune in unison for one stanza, then music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Next one man as Music-King Bodhisattva held a flower-bridle slight drum; all danced one stanza of the preceding tune, then music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次婦女三人，歌《新水令》、《沽美酒》、《太平令》之曲終，念口號畢，舞唱相和，以次而出。

translations.literal: Next three women sang through the tunes "New Water Order," "Buy Fine Wine," and "Peace Order"; when the slogans were finished they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: Next three women sang "New Water Order," "Buy Fine Wine," and "Peace Order"; after the slogans they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 壽星隊：

translations.literal: Longevity Star Troupe:
translations.idiomatic: Longevity Star Troupe:

sentences.zh: （天壽節用之。）〉

translations.literal: (Used at the Heavenly Longevity Festival.)
translations.idiomatic: (Used at the Heavenly Longevity Festival.)

sentences.zh: 引隊禮官樂工大樂冠服，並同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: Leading ceremonial officers and Great Music caps and dress all the same as the Music-King Troupe.
translations.idiomatic: Leading officers and Great Music dress matched the Music-King Troupe.

sentences.zh: 次二隊，婦女十人，冠唐巾，服銷金紫衣，銅束帶。

translations.literal: Next the second troupe: ten women wearing Tang caps, gold-brocade purple clothes, bronze belts.
translations.idiomatic: The second troupe: ten women in Tang caps, gold-brocade purple robes, bronze belts.

sentences.zh: 次婦女一人，冠平天冠，服繡鶴氅，方心曲領，執圭，以次進至御前，立定，樂止，念致語畢，樂作，奏《長春柳》之曲。

translations.literal: Next one woman wearing a Level Heaven cap, embroidered crane mantle, square heart curved collar, holding a scepter, advancing in order to before the emperor and standing fixed; music stopped; when the congratulatory address was finished, music played, performing the tune "Long Spring Willow."
translations.idiomatic: Next one woman in a Level Heaven cap, embroidered crane mantle, square heart curved collar, scepter in hand, advanced to the imperial presence; music stopped; after the address music played "Long Spring Willow."

sentences.zh: 次三隊，男子三人，冠服舞蹈，並同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: Next the third troupe: three men, caps, dress, and dance all the same as the Music-King Troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The third troupe: three men in caps, dress, and dance as the Music-King Troupe.

sentences.zh: 次四隊，男子一人，冠金漆弁冠，服緋袍，塗金帶，執笏；

translations.literal: Next the fourth troupe: one man wearing a gold-lacquer cap, scarlet robe, gilded belt, holding a tablet;
translations.idiomatic: The fourth troupe: one man in a gold-lacquer cap, scarlet robe, gilded belt, tablet in hand;

sentences.zh: 從者二人，錦帽，繡衣，執金字福祿牌。

translations.literal: two followers, brocade caps, embroidered clothes, holding gold-character fortune-and-emolument plaques.
translations.idiomatic: two followers in brocade caps and embroidered dress holding gold-character fortune plaques.

sentences.zh: 次五隊，男子一人，冠卷雲冠，青面具，綠袍，塗金帶，分執梅、竹、松、椿、石，同前隊而進，北向立。

translations.literal: Next the fifth troupe: one man wearing a coiling-cloud cap, green mask, green robe, gilded belt, separately holding plum, bamboo, pine, camellia, and stone; advancing like the preceding troupe, standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth troupe: one man in a coiling-cloud cap, green mask, green robe, gilded belt, holding plum, bamboo, pine, camellia, and stone, advanced like the preceding troupe and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 次六隊，男子五人，為烏鴉之像，作飛舞之態，進立於前隊之左，樂止。

translations.literal: Next the sixth troupe: five men as crow images in flying-dancing posture, advancing to stand to the left of the preceding troupe; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth troupe: five men as crows in flying dance advanced to stand left of the preceding troupe; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次七隊，樂工十有二人，冠雲頭冠，銷金緋袍，白裙，龍笛三，觱栗三，劄鼓三，和鼓一，板一，與前大樂合奏《山荊子》帶《妖神急》之曲。

translations.literal: Next the seventh troupe: twelve musicians wearing cloud-head caps, gold-brocade scarlet robes, white skirts; three dragon flutes, three suona, three zha drums, one he drum, one clapper, joining the preceding Great Music in performing the tune "Mountain Thorn" with "Demon Spirit Urgent."
translations.idiomatic: The seventh troupe: twelve musicians in cloud-head caps, gold-brocade scarlet robes, white skirts; three dragon flutes, three suona, three zha drums, one he drum, one clapper, joining the Great Music in "Mountain Thorn" with "Demon Spirit Urgent."

sentences.zh: 次八隊，婦女二十人，冠鳳翹冠，翠花鈿，服寬袖衣，加雲肩、霞綬、玉佩，各執寶蓋，舞唱前曲。

translations.literal: Next the eighth troupe: twenty women wearing phoenix-crest caps, kingfisher hairpins, wide-sleeved clothes with cloud collars, rosy sashes, and jade pendants, each holding a treasure canopy, dancing and singing the preceding tune.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth troupe: twenty women in phoenix-crest caps, kingfisher hairpins, wide sleeves with cloud collars, rosy sashes, jade pendants, treasure canopies in hand, dancing and singing the preceding tune.

sentences.zh: 次九隊，婦女三十人，冠玉女冠，翠花鈿，服黃銷金寬袖衣，加雲肩、霞綬、玉佩，各執棕毛日月扇，舞唱前曲，與前隊相和。

translations.literal: Next the ninth troupe: thirty women wearing Jade Maiden caps, kingfisher hairpins, yellow gold-brocade wide-sleeved clothes with cloud collars, rosy sashes, jade pendants, each holding palm-leaf sun-and-moon fans, dancing and singing the preceding tune in harmony with the preceding troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth troupe: thirty women in Jade Maiden caps, yellow gold-brocade wide sleeves, cloud collars, rosy sashes, jade pendants, palm sun-and-moon fans, dancing and singing with the preceding troupe.

sentences.zh: 次十隊，婦女八人，服雜彩衣，被槲葉、魚鼓、簡子。

translations.literal: Next the tenth troupe: eight women wearing mixed-color clothes, carrying oak leaves, fish drums, and bamboo clappers.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth troupe: eight women in mixed-color dress with oak leaves, fish drums, and bamboo clappers.

sentences.zh: 次男子八人，冠束發冠，金掩心甲，銷金緋袍，執戟。

translations.literal: Next eight men wearing bound-hair caps, golden heart-protecting armor, gold-brocade scarlet robes, holding halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Next eight men in bound-hair caps, golden heart-protecting armor, gold-brocade scarlet robes, halberds in hand.

sentences.zh: 次為龜鶴之像各一。

translations.literal: Next one tortoise image and one crane image each.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one tortoise image and one crane image.

sentences.zh: 次男子五人，冠黑紗帽，服繡鶴氅，朱履，策龍頭濆杖，齊舞唱前曲一闋，樂止。

translations.literal: Next five men wearing black gauze caps, embroidered crane mantles, red shoes, grasping dragon-head sprinkling staffs, all dancing and singing one stanza of the preceding tune in unison; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Next five men in black gauze caps, embroidered crane mantles, red shoes, dragon-head sprinkling staffs, danced one stanza in unison; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次婦女三人，歌《新水令》、《沽美酒》、《太平令》之曲終，念口號畢，舞唱相和，以次而出。

translations.literal: Next three women sang through the tunes "New Water Order," "Buy Fine Wine," and "Peace Order"; when the slogans were finished they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: Next three women sang "New Water Order," "Buy Fine Wine," and "Peace Order"; after the slogans they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 禮樂隊：

translations.literal: Rites Music Troupe:
translations.idiomatic: Rites Music Troupe:

sentences.zh: （朝會用之。）〉

translations.literal: (Used at court assemblies.)
translations.idiomatic: (Used at court assemblies.)

sentences.zh: 引隊禮官樂工大樂冠服，並同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: Leading ceremonial officers and Great Music caps and dress all the same as the Music-King Troupe.
translations.idiomatic: Leading officers and Great Music dress matched the Music-King Troupe.

sentences.zh: 次二隊，婦女十人，冠黑漆弁冠，服青素袍，方心曲領，白裙，束帶，執圭；

translations.literal: Next the second troupe: ten women wearing black-lacquer caps, blue plain robes, square heart curved collar, white skirts, belts, holding scepters;
translations.idiomatic: The second troupe: ten women in black-lacquer caps, blue plain robes, square heart curved collar, white skirts, belts, scepters in hand;

sentences.zh: 次婦女一人，冠九龍冠，服繡紅袍，玉束帶，進至御前，立定，樂止，念致語畢，樂作，奏《長春柳》之曲。

translations.literal: next one woman wearing a Nine Dragons cap, embroidered red robe, jade belt, advancing to before the emperor and standing fixed; music stopped; when the congratulatory address was finished, music played, performing the tune "Long Spring Willow."
translations.idiomatic: next one woman in a Nine Dragons cap, embroidered red robe, jade belt, advanced to the imperial presence; music stopped; after the address music played "Long Spring Willow."

sentences.zh: 次三隊，男子三人，冠服舞蹈同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: Next the third troupe: three men, caps, dress, and dance the same as the Music-King Troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The third troupe: three men in caps, dress, and dance as the Music-King Troupe.

sentences.zh: 次四隊，男子三人，皆冠卷雲冠，服黃袍，塗金帶，執圭。

translations.literal: Next the fourth troupe: three men, all wearing coiling-cloud caps, yellow robes, gilded belts, holding scepters.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth troupe: three men in coiling-cloud caps, yellow robes, gilded belts, scepters in hand.

sentences.zh: 次五隊，男子五人，皆冠三龍冠，服紅袍，各執劈正金斧，同前隊而進，北向立。

translations.literal: Next the fifth troupe: five men, all wearing Three Dragons caps, red robes, each holding a gold-inlaid correction axe; advancing like the preceding troupe, standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth troupe: five men in Three Dragons caps, red robes, each with a gold-inlaid correction axe, advanced like the preceding troupe and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 次六隊，童子五人，三髻，素衣，各執香花，舞蹈而進，樂止。

translations.literal: Next the sixth troupe: five boys, triple topknots, plain clothes, each holding incense flowers, dancing forward; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth troupe: five boys with triple topknots in plain clothes, incense flowers in hand, danced forward; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次七隊，樂工八人，皆冠束發冠，服錦衣白袍，龍笛三，觱栗三，杖鼓二，與前大樂合奏《新水令》、《水仙子》之曲。

translations.literal: Next the seventh troupe: eight musicians, all wearing bound-hair caps, brocade white robes; three dragon flutes, three suona, two zhang drums, joining the preceding Great Music in performing the tunes "New Water Order" and "Water Immortal."
translations.idiomatic: The seventh troupe: eight musicians in bound-hair caps and brocade white robes; three dragon flutes, three suona, two zhang drums, joining the Great Music in "New Water Order" and "Water Immortal."

sentences.zh: 次八隊，婦女二十人，冠籠巾，服紫袍，金帶，執笏，歌《新水令》之曲，與樂聲相和，進至御前，分為四行，北向立，鞠躬拜，興，舞蹈，叩頭，山呼，就拜，再拜，畢，復趁聲歌《水仙子》之曲一闋，再歌《青山口》之曲，與後隊相和。

translations.literal: Next the eighth troupe: twenty women wearing cage caps, purple robes, gold belts, holding tablets, singing the tune "New Water Order" in harmony with the music, advancing to before the emperor, dividing into four rows, standing facing north, bowing with bent waist, rising, dancing, kowtowing, shouting "ten thousand years," performing the bow, bowing again; when finished, again following the sound singing one stanza of "Water Immortal," then again singing "Green Mountain Pass" in harmony with the following troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth troupe: twenty women in cage caps, purple robes, gold belts, tablets in hand, sang "New Water Order" with the music, advanced to the imperial presence in four rows facing north, bowed, rose, danced, kowtowed, shouted "ten thousand years," bowed again; then sang "Water Immortal" and "Green Mountain Pass" with the following troupe.

sentences.zh: 次九隊，婦女二十人，冠車髻冠，服銷金藍衣，雲肩，佩綬，執孔雀幢，舞唱與前隊相和。

translations.literal: Next the ninth troupe: twenty women wearing carriage-topknot caps, gold-brocade blue clothes, cloud collars, sash pendants, holding peacock banners, dancing and singing in harmony with the preceding troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth troupe: twenty women in carriage-topknot caps, gold-brocade blue dress, cloud collars, sash pendants, peacock banners, dancing and singing with the preceding troupe.

sentences.zh: 次十隊，婦女八人，冠翠花唐巾，服錦繡衣，執寶蓋，舞唱前曲。

translations.literal: Next the tenth troupe: eight women wearing kingfisher floral Tang caps, brocade embroidered clothes, holding treasure canopies, dancing and singing the preceding tune.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth troupe: eight women in kingfisher floral Tang caps, brocade dress, treasure canopies, dancing and singing the preceding tune.

sentences.zh: 次男子八人，冠鳳翅兜牟，披金甲，執金戟。

translations.literal: Next eight men wearing phoenix-wing helmets, clad in golden armor, holding golden halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Next eight men in phoenix-wing helmets, golden armor, golden halberds.

sentences.zh: 次男子一人，冠平天冠，服繡鶴氅，執圭，齊舞唱前曲一闋，樂止。

translations.literal: Next one man wearing a Level Heaven cap, embroidered crane mantle, holding a scepter; all danced and sang one stanza of the preceding tune in unison; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Next one man in a Level Heaven cap and embroidered crane mantle, scepter in hand; all danced one stanza; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次婦女三人，歌《新水令》、《沽美酒》、《太平令》之曲終，念口號畢，舞唱相和，以次而出。

translations.literal: Next three women sang through the tunes "New Water Order," "Buy Fine Wine," and "Peace Order"; when the slogans were finished they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: Next three women sang "New Water Order," "Buy Fine Wine," and "Peace Order"; after the slogans they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 說法隊：引隊禮官樂工大樂冠服，並同樂音王隊。
