translations.literal: Dharma-Teaching Troupe: leading ceremonial officers and Great Music caps and dress all the same as the Music-King Troupe.
translations.idiomatic: Dharma-Teaching Troupe: leading officers and Great Music dress matched the Music-King Troupe.

sentences.zh: 次二隊，婦女十人，冠僧伽帽，服紫禪衣，皂絳；

translations.literal: Next the second troupe: ten women wearing Sangha caps, purple monastic robes, black borders;
translations.idiomatic: The second troupe: ten women in Sangha caps, purple monastic robes, black borders;

sentences.zh: 次婦女一人，服錦袈裟，余如前，持數珠，進至御前，北向立定，樂止，念致語畢，樂作，奏《長春柳》之曲。

translations.literal: next one woman wearing a brocade kasaya, the rest as before, holding prayer beads, advancing to before the emperor, standing facing north fixed; music stopped; when the congratulatory address was finished, music played, performing the tune "Long Spring Willow."
translations.idiomatic: next one woman in a brocade kasaya as before, prayer beads in hand, advanced to the imperial presence facing north; music stopped; after the address music played "Long Spring Willow."

sentences.zh: 次三隊，男子三人，冠、服、舞蹈，並同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: Next the third troupe: three men, caps, dress, and dance all the same as the Music-King Troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The third troupe: three men in caps, dress, and dance as the Music-King Troupe.

sentences.zh: 次四隊，男子一人，冠隱士冠，服白紗道袍，皂絳，執麈拂；

translations.literal: Next the fourth troupe: one man wearing a recluse cap, white gauze Daoist robe, black border, holding a fly-whisk;
translations.idiomatic: The fourth troupe: one man in a recluse cap, white gauze Daoist robe, black border, fly-whisk in hand;

sentences.zh: 從者二人，冠黃包巾，服錦繡衣，執令字旗。

translations.literal: two followers wearing yellow wrapped caps, brocade embroidered clothes, holding command-character banners.
translations.idiomatic: two followers in yellow wrapped caps and brocade dress holding command-character banners.

sentences.zh: 次五隊，男子五人，冠金冠，披金甲，錦袍，執戟，同前隊而進，北向立。

translations.literal: Next the fifth troupe: five men wearing gold caps, clad in golden armor, brocade robes, holding halberds; advancing like the preceding troupe, standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth troupe: five men in gold caps, golden armor, brocade robes, halberds in hand, advanced like the preceding troupe and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 次六隊，男子五人，為金翅雕之像，舞蹈而進，樂止。

translations.literal: Next the sixth troupe: five men as golden-winged eagle images, dancing forward; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth troupe: five men as golden-winged eagles danced forward; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次七隊，樂工十有六人，冠五福冠，服錦繡衣，龍笛六，觱栗六，杖鼓四，與前大樂合奏《金字西番經》之曲。

translations.literal: Next the seventh troupe: sixteen musicians wearing Five Blessings caps, brocade embroidered clothes; six dragon flutes, six suona, four zhang drums, joining the preceding Great Music in performing the tune "Gold-Character Western Barbarian Scripture."
translations.idiomatic: The seventh troupe: sixteen musicians in Five Blessings caps and brocade dress; six dragon flutes, six suona, four zhang drums, joining the Great Music in "Gold-Character Western Barbarian Scripture."

sentences.zh: 次八隊，婦女二十人，冠珠子菩薩冠，服銷金黃衣，纓絡，佩綬，執金浮屠白傘蓋，舞唱前曲，與樂聲相和，進至御前，分為五重，重四人，曲終，再起，與後隊相和。

translations.literal: Next the eighth troupe: twenty women wearing bead Bodhisattva caps, gold-brocade yellow clothes, tassels, sash pendants, holding golden pagoda white umbrellas, dancing and singing the preceding tune in harmony with the music, advancing to before the emperor, divided into five ranks of four each; when the tune ended they rose again to harmonize with the following troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth troupe: twenty women in bead Bodhisattva caps, gold-brocade yellow robes, tassels, sash pendants, golden pagoda white umbrellas, danced and sang the preceding tune, advanced in five ranks of four; at the tune's end they rose to meet the following troupe.

sentences.zh: 次九隊，婦女二十人，冠金翠菩薩冠，服銷金紅衣，執寶蓋，舞唱與前隊相和。

translations.literal: Next the ninth troupe: twenty women wearing gold-kingfisher Bodhisattva caps, gold-brocade red clothes, holding treasure canopies, dancing and singing in harmony with the preceding troupe.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth troupe: twenty women in gold-kingfisher Bodhisattva caps, gold-brocade red robes, treasure canopies, dancing and singing with the preceding troupe.

sentences.zh: 次十隊，婦女八人，冠青螺髻冠，服白銷金衣，執金蓮花。

translations.literal: Next the tenth troupe: eight women wearing blue-snail topknot caps, white gold-brocade clothes, holding golden lotus flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth troupe: eight women in blue-snail topknot caps, white gold-brocade robes, golden lotuses in hand.

sentences.zh: 次男子八人，披金甲，為八金剛像。

translations.literal: Next eight men clad in golden armor as Eight Vajra images.
translations.idiomatic: Next eight men in golden armor as the Eight Vajras.

sentences.zh: 次一人，為文殊像，執如意；

translations.literal: Next one man as a Manjusri image, holding a ruyi scepter;
translations.idiomatic: Next one man as Manjusri, ruyi in hand;

sentences.zh: 一人為普賢像，執西番蓮花；

translations.literal: one man as a Samantabhadra image, holding a Western lotus;
translations.idiomatic: one as Samantabhadra, Western lotus in hand;

sentences.zh: 一人為如來像；

translations.literal: one man as a Tathagata image;
translations.idiomatic: one as the Tathagata;

sentences.zh: 齊舞唱前曲一闋，樂止。

translations.literal: all danced and sang one stanza of the preceding tune in unison; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: all danced one stanza in unison; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次婦女三人，歌《新水令》、《沽美酒》、《太平令》之曲終，念口號畢，舞唱相和，以次而出。

translations.literal: Next three women sang through the tunes "New Water Order," "Buy Fine Wine," and "Peace Order"; when the slogans were finished they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: Next three women sang "New Water Order," "Buy Fine Wine," and "Peace Order"; after the slogans they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 凡吉禮，郊祀、享太廟、告謚，見《祭祀志》。

translations.literal: For auspicious rites generally—suburban sacrifices, offerings at the Grand Temple, posthumous title announcements—see the Treatise on Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: For auspicious rites—suburban sacrifices, Grand Temple offerings, posthumous title announcements—see the Treatise on Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 軍禮，見《兵志》。

translations.literal: Military rites, see the Treatise on Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Military rites are treated in the Treatise on Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 喪禮五服，見《刑法志》。

translations.literal: Mourning rites and five grades of mourning dress, see the Treatise on Punishment and Law.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites and the five grades of mourning dress appear in the Treatise on Punishment and Law.

sentences.zh: 水旱賑恤，見《食貨志》。

translations.literal: Flood, drought, and relief, see the Treatise on Food and Goods.
translations.idiomatic: Flood, drought, and relief are covered in the Treatise on Food and Goods.

sentences.zh: 內外導從，見《儀衛志》。

translations.literal: Inner and outer escorts, see the Treatise on Ceremonial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer escorts are described in the Treatise on Ceremonial Guards.
